attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov et al. (2026) on dandiset 001515, which holds FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses of CHO cells charged by single 1-us pulses at one amplitude per cell. None of the paper's experiments (sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns with field escalation, Di-8-ANEPPS, 0.3-us pulses, Gd3+, two-pulse and Ca2+ recordings) is in it, so 33 of 34 claims are blocked; the one computation from the paper's Eq. (2) is tested. The notebook checks what the files hold.

outcomes.statement: Below and near the electroporation threshold (43 to 570 V/cm, 1-us pulses), the membrane depolarizes at the cathode-facing pole and hyperpolarizes at the anode-facing pole, polarization decreases from the poles towards the equator, and it scales proportionally with field strength, as the Schwan equation describes.
outcomes.quote: Electric pulses below and near the electroporation threshold produce a well-known spatial pattern of membrane polarization, such as in Fig. 1, 43–570 V/cm. The membrane depolarizes at the cathode-facing membrane pole and hyperpolarizes at the opposite, anode-facing pole. Polarization gradually decreases from the poles towards the cell equator, and scales up proportionally with the electric field strength
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 292 files of FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses (70 frames each, one 1-us pulse amplitude per subject, 20 to 100 V across electrodes 1.00 mm apart, frame delays not recorded). The claim needs Di-8-ANEPPS recordings; every file is FluoVolt. It also needs the paper's escalation sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns, which no file has. Dandisets 001516, 001517 and 001518 also name this paper and may hold these data; they are separate targets of the registry and were not read here.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims, and at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator stay polarized and may polarize more than the poles.
outcomes.source: Figure 1 and its legend; Results 3.1, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles ... while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 292 files of FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses (70 frames each, one 1-us pulse amplitude per subject, 20 to 100 V across electrodes 1.00 mm apart, frame delays not recorded). outcomes.statement: With FluoVolt, pole dF rose with field strength until it saturated at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
outcomes.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 292 files of FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses (70 frames each, one 1-us pulse amplitude per subject, 20 to 100 V across electrodes 1.00 mm apart, frame delays not recorded). The claim needs the FluoVolt experiments of the paper, sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns into 1-us pulses with the field escalated from 43 to 1400 V/cm within each cell (n = 4); no file has that structure, and no cell is exposed to more than one amplitude. Using the dandiset's time courses in their place would also need the delay of each frame (to find the 900-ns frame) and the field strength in V/cm (the paper's comes from a Sim4Life model of 1.6-mm electrodes), neither of which the files record, so this is also metadata_insufficient. Dandisets 001516, 001517 and 001518 also name this paper and may hold these data; they are separate targets of the registry and were not read here.

outcomes.statement: By Eq. (2), the effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold rise reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold rise by 12%.
outcomes.quote: its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%.
outcomes.notes: Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives an IMP reduction of 1.33% (reading a, 1 - f/1.5) or 1.20% (reading b, relative to f at 3e-7 S/m) for a 10-fold rise of membrane conductivity, outside 2 +- 0.2%, and 11.87% (a) or 11.75% (b) for a 100-fold rise, inside 12 +- 1.2%. Both readings give the same result. The qualitative part of the statement holds, as a 1000-fold rise is needed to reduce IMP by more than half (57.4%). In a grid of radii 5 to 15 um and membrane thicknesses 3 to 7 nm (a variant, not the criterion), no combination puts both values within tolerance under reading (a); R = 8 um with d = 3 nm gives 2.19% and 18.3%. The computation uses no recordings.
deviations: None in method; Eq. (2) and its constants are those of Methods 2.3, and both readings of the criterion were run.

outcomes.statement: A single 1-us pulse caused clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through 5 min; the small rise at 780 V/cm was not significant.

A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 292 files of FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses (70 frames each, one 1-us pulse amplitude per subject, 20 to 100 V across electrodes 1.00 mm apart, frame delays not recorded). findings.statement: The dandiset names this paper (IsPublishedIn) but holds none of its recordings. Its 292 files are FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses at one 1-us pulse amplitude per cell, the protocol the paper attributes to its reference [20] (Semenov et al. 2025, Bioelectrochemistry 168, 109143). The paper's sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns with field escalation, and its Di-8-ANEPPS, 0.3-us, Gd3+, two-pulse and Fluo-4 Ca2+ recordings, are absent, so 33 of the 34 claims cannot be tested.

The laser delay of each frame is not recorded; the files give only a start time and a nominal 6 Hz. The data show that the 70 frames are successive delays across the pulse (the response rises and falls over a median 19 frames at half peak, at frames 16 to 34 in forward files and at the same frames counted from the end in backward files), so the backward files hold the time course in reverse order. A step of about 50 ns is consistent with this but not shown.

Pulses are given in volts across electrodes stated as 1.00 mm apart; no field strength is given. The paper uses electrodes 1.6 mm apart and field strengths from Sim4Life modelling, so its V/cm values cannot be assigned to these files. At the same 40 V the response differs between sessions (median peak index 25.9% on 2023-05-08, 11.9% on 2023-09-26).

Each subject has two files for each combination of recording order (forward, backward) and anode side, with nothing in the files to tell the two apart. Subject CHO-20230925-c1 has 4 files where the others have 8. Each file images a field of several cells (2 to 12 connected parts of the membrane mask; touching cells form one part), while the paper analyses one cell per experiment; no file says which cell, if any, the subject is.

File sub-CHO-20230926-c1_obj-bcvqko shows a different field of view from the other files of its subject (median correlation of mean images 0.079, against 0.995 for files of one subject) and a session start of 2024-12-16, fourteen months after that subject's other files. Its response is weak (peak index 1.3%).

The stated anode side does not fix the sign of the response. In 35 of 37 subjects the sign flips between the files stated as anode above and below, but 9 files differ in sign from the majority of the other files of their subject with the same stated anode side (groups with a tied majority are not counted), and across sessions files stated as anode above are brighter at the top of the cells (2023-05-08) or at the bottom (2023-09-25, 2023-09-26), and both in different subjects of 2023-10-10. The image orientation relative to the electrodes is not stated.
In 220 of 292 files frame 0 is less than 0.8 times as bright as the median frame (median ratio 0.59), which the description does not explain.

The archive summary gives the species as 'Cricetulus griseus - Cricetulus aureus' for a CHO cell line (the files give NCBITaxon_10029, C. griseus only), and every subject has an age of P1D. The image series description mentions sine wave exposures, which no file holds.

Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 gives a 1.33% IMP reduction for a 10-fold rise of membrane conductivity, where Results 3.5 states about 2%; the 100-fold value (11.87%) matches the stated 12%.

entries.name: 001515-semenov-2026
entries.title: Membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields (Semenov et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov et al. (2026) on dandiset 001515, which holds FluoVolt strobe-imaging time courses of CHO cells charged by single 1-us pulses at one amplitude per cell. None of the paper's experiments (sets of 40 baseline and 60 pulse images at 900 ns with field escalation, Di-8-ANEPPS, 0.3-us pulses, Gd3+, two-pulse and Ca2+ recordings) is in it, so 33 of 34 claims are blocked; the one computation from the paper's Eq. (2) is tested. The notebook checks what the files hold.
